column3: According to the Google SRE book, a monitoring system designed on the mean latency hides the tail: with an average latency of 100 ms at 1,000 requests per second, 1% of requests might easily take 5 seconds.
If users depend on several such services to render their page, the book says the 99th percentile of one backend can easily become the median response of the frontend.
According to the same chapter, the simplest way to tell a slow average from a very slow tail is to collect request counts bucketed by latency, which suit a histogram, instead of the actual latencies.
It suggests distributing the histogram boundaries approximately exponentially, in its example by factors of roughly 3.

According to the same chapter, latency is one of the four golden signals of monitoring, and it is important to track the latency of failed requests as well as that of successful ones, because a slow error is even worse than a fast error.
The chapter also says that measuring the 99th percentile response time over a small window, for example one minute, can give a very early signal of saturation.
